newsitem.title: UK: UK inflation falls to 2.4 percent in April.
newsitem.headline: UK inflation falls to 2.4 percent in April.

text.p: British retail prices rose 0.6 percent in April to give an annual inflation rate of 2.4 percent, down from 2.6 percent in March, official figures showed on Thursday.
The price data were slightly better than analysts had expected.
"The figures are definitely somewhat better than expected," said Glenn Davies, chief economist at Credit Lyonnais.

The inflation rate excluding mortgage interest payments fell to 2.5 percent in April from 2.7 percent. This index is closely watched by the government which aims to keep inflation at 2.5 percent or less over the medium term.
Sterling was steady after the data at 2.7825 marks while the stock market shrugged off the figures.
"The short term outlook for inflation remains stable with the strength of sterling keeping a lid on prices," said Philip Shaw, economist at Union Plc.
